cards.explanation: The answer is the good things to come. The writer says the law is “…only a shadow of the good things to come, not the realities themselves.” A shadow of a cookie on the counter tells you a cookie is near, but nobody ever got fed by the shadow. The law points ahead to something better, friends.

The answer is False. The writer says the law can never, by the same sacrifices offered year after year, “…make perfect those who draw near to worship.” The law is a shadow, and a shadow can't do the job of the real thing. Year after year the same sacrifices keep coming, and they still can't make anyone perfect, friends.

The answer is that they would have stopped. The writer asks, “If it could, would not the offerings have ceased?” Think about it, friends. When a job is truly finished, you quit doing it. The offerings kept going, and that tells us they couldn't do the job.

The answer is reminder. The writer says, “Instead, those sacrifices are an annual reminder of sins…” Every year they brought the sins back to mind instead of ending them, friends. It's like a bill that shows up in the mailbox every year, a reminder that it's still there.

The answer is that God did not desire them. When Christ came into the world, He said, “Sacrifice and offering You did not desire…” (Hebrews 10:5) He is speaking to God here, friends. Then He adds that God took no delight in burnt offerings and sin offerings. (Hebrews 10:6)

The answer is to do God's will. Christ says, “Here I am, I have come to do Your will.” (Hebrews 10:9) He also says it is written about Him in the scroll. I like a mission with a clear job description, friends, and this one is the clearest there is.

The answer is True. After replaying Christ's words, the writer adds a note in parentheses: “(although they are offered according to the law).” So he's telling us the sacrifices were offered according to the law, even though God did not desire them, friends. A little side note, and it matters.

The answer is once. The writer says we have been sanctified through the sacrifice of the body of Jesus Christ “…once for all…” One time, friends, not year after year and not day after day. That's the difference from the sacrifices the priests kept offering (Hebrews 10:1, 11).

The answer is that He sat down at God's right hand. The writer says that when this Priest had offered for all time one sacrifice for sins, “…He sat down at the right hand of God.” Compare that to the priests, who stand day after day to offer the same sacrifices again and again, friends. (Hebrews 10:11) One Priest sits, and the others keep standing.

The answer is True. The writer says, “Since that time, He waits for His enemies to be made a footstool for His feet…” So after sitting down at the right hand of God, Jesus waits. That's why my ovens stay ready, friends, though the text never says when.

The answer is perfect. The writer says, “…by a single offering He has made perfect for all time those who are being sanctified.” One offering, friends, and the result is for all time. That's the same one sacrifice the writer pointed to in verse 12.

The answer is in their hearts and minds. The Lord says, “I will put My laws in their hearts and inscribe them on their minds.” The writer says these words come from the Holy Spirit's testimony, friends. The laws go inside, to the heart and the mind.

The answer is False. The Lord says, “Their sins and lawless acts I will remember no more.” That is a big change, friends, from the sacrifices that served as “…an annual reminder of sins…” (Hebrews 10:3) Not remembered, not even once a year.

The answer is an offering for sin. The writer says, “And where these have been forgiven, an offering for sin is no longer needed.” When sins are forgiven, friends, there's nothing left to offer for them. That ties it all together, and I'm happy to let it be the last word.
